pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds a NOT NULL column with default 'normal' and a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. I did not run it.
The item() function in src/index.js appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list items.
src/index.js binds priority in 'WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id'. The 'AC-3' test checks high, low and normal filters, including id order.
With no filter the query is 'SELECT title, priority FROM items ORDER BY id'. The 'AC-4' test covers it.
nav() renders All, High, Normal and Low on every view, with the current one in <strong> and the rest as links. The 'AC-5' test asserts the full nav string for all four views.

searchParams.has('priority') combined with a Set membership check returns 400 for any other value, including an empty value. The 'AC-6' test covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks that no <li> is returned.
The empty message is 'No {priority}-priority items.' only when the table is non-empty, and 'No items yet.' otherwise. The 'AC-7' test covers no match and an empty table in all four views.

traffic/routes.json is ["/", "/?priority=high"]. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. The traffic worker requests every route with its query (`https://app.internal${path}`). scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts a query string, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers both the accepted and refused cases.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions. Existing items default to normal and only high and low are labelled. Nothing was added beyond the spec, except the traffic-config-check relaxation that AC-8 needs; the PR discloses it.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and have tests that assert behaviour. The tests were not executed in this review because the shell refused them.

The new tests assert rendered output and statuses. The only existing test changed is the fake app in test/traffic.test.js, which now records the query string; no assertion was loosened. I could not run the suite.
README.md describes the ?priority filter. No docs are stale.
The priority is bound as a parameter. 400 handling and the empty-state logic are correct. No dead code.
The priority value is checked against an allow-list before the query. Titles are still HTML-escaped, and the priority output is limited to the allowed values. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no styling or design files; the page is a plain server-rendered list with a nav line, and the spec's states table is covered under spec.
No browser or UI flow was available in this review; behaviour was checked through the Worker tests, which I read but did not run.

The title and body match the diff: the 400 behaviour, the labels, the migration, the routes.json entry and the traffic-check relaxation. The CI and reviewer claims can't be checked from the repository.
